_no_subject_profile: Deliberate: this recipe does NOT declare subject_profile. A profile would auto-wire an IP-Adapter face reference, and a reference plus a LoRA is two identity sources — you could no longer tell which one produced the face. The probe must isolate ONE variable: the LoRA's own weights. (It also means this runs on the plain t2i graph, which has no LoadImage node.)
_note: THE DECISIVE DIAGNOSTIC. Plain SD1.5 text-to-image: no target, no mask, no mesh, no img2img. Just the checkpoint + the Carey LoRA + the trigger phrase, drawing a face from scratch. This is the ONLY configuration in which an identity LoRA can express facial GEOMETRY, and until 2026-07-25 no recipe in this repo ran it — every LoRA recipe was a target-edit (anime_face_edit, anime_face_zone_edit v1/v2/v3), where the mesh/mask pins geometry to the target before the LoRA can contribute. That is why ~8 trained LoRAs produced no measurable progress. Run this FIRST. It answers one question: does the trained LoRA carry Carey at all? Everything downstream depends on that answer.
_require_exact_checkpoint_note: A diagnostic must never silently swap models. If 'meina' is absent, byrdimage's normal fallback could hand this SD1.5 LoRA an SDXL checkpoint; the result is mush in every cell, which reads as 'the LoRA never learned the face' and sends you into an unnecessary multi-day retrain. Fail loudly instead.

identity._note: SD1.5 pack. The trigger phrase MUST appear in the prompt or the adapter barely fires — prepare-carey-lora-dataset.py captions every training image with 'careybh person'.

template: careybh person, {shot} of an adult Black man, {expression}, {lighting}, plain neutral background, sharp focus on the face, detailed facial features, photograph
negative: cartoon, anime, illustration, painting, 3d render, cgi, doll, plastic skin, deformed face, distorted features, extra faces, multiple people, blurry, low quality, watermark, text, hat, sunglasses

expression.default: neutral expression, looking straight at the camera
expression.label: Expression

rubric.identity: 1-5 — is this recognizably Carey compared to the REAL reference photos? 1 = a generic man, 5 = unmistakably him. This is the only score that matters here.
rubric.face_integrity: 1-5 — coherent eyes/mouth/jaw, no melting or doubled features
rubric.realism: 1-5 — reads as a photograph, not a render
